llm.summary: This skill is for TikTok Shop refund lookups, but it exposes a broader authenticated proxy that could call more shop APIs than the narrow description suggests.

dimensions.detail: Outbound calls to the LinkFox TikTok gateway and use of openId/API-key context are expected for this integration, but an arbitrary method/path proxy over broad API prefixes is not proportionate to a single reject-reasons skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time persistence or package installation was found. Runtime use depends on Python scripts, environment API keys, the LinkFox gateway, and the linkfox-tiktok-shop-auth dependency; metadata does not declare these capabilities.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill trigger and description are narrow and say authorization is not included, but SKILL.md and scripts document a broader path whitelist and generic path/method execution under an ERP openId context.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not write files or install background workers, but it can use LINKFOX_AGENT_API_KEY and backend ERP token context through openId; shop_cipher can be auto-resolved for return_refund paths.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose centers on Get Reject Reasons, while the artifacts also expose get_authorized_shops and a generic developerProxy wrapper for return_refund/ and authorization/ paths with caller-controlled method, query, and body.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This does not show destructive or deceptive behavior, but it gives an agent authenticated ERP gateway access beyond a single reject-reasons lookup. Install only if you are comfortable with generic return_refund/authorization proxy capability under your TikTok Shop LinkFox authorization, or ask the publisher to remove the generic proxy and limit the skill to the documented read-only endpoint.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The shell, environment-variable, and network behavior is expected for a script-based LinkFox API skill, but the empty metadata under-discloses those runtime needs.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifact presents a narrow reject-reasons skill while documenting and implementing broader authorized-shop lookup and generic developerProxy functionality.
[SDI-1] expected: The authorized-shops API is purpose-adjacent because shop_cipher is needed for shop-scoped refund APIs, but exposing it as a standalone operation conflicts with the description saying authorization is not included.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The generic proxy in _return_refund_api_runner.py is materially broader than the declared Get Reject Reasons operation and accepts caller-controlled path, method, query, and body.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The arbitrary proxy increases the reachable API surface beyond the documented read-only reject-reasons workflow, including possible state-changing return_refund calls if accepted by the upstream gateway.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Auto-resolving shop_cipher is expected for the named reject-reasons call, but doing it inside the generic proxy obscures when shop-scoped authority is being applied.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The shared allowlist permits broad return_refund and authorization prefixes rather than only the specific reject-reasons endpoint needed for this skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The return_refund_proxy usage text openly advertises generic path/method proxying, confirming the broader capability rather than a scanner-only inference.
